text:
customer-ops: Hey @maya-support, heads up — our March invoice is ~18% higher than the dashboard/SDK estimates. Local SDK run for a day shows ~1,200,000 tokens but invoice line shows ~1,420,000. Not seeing any unusual traffic on our side. Any pointers?

maya-support: Thanks — can you paste a sample request (redact keys) and a request_id from one affected call? Also which SDK version?

customer-ops: SDK v1.4.2. Here's a sanitized curl for one of the calls we think is representative:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-v1-large","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a concise summarizer."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following logs..."},{"role":"tool","name":"kv_prefill","content":"{\"session_id\":\"s-9823\",\"user_meta\":\"...\"}"}],"stream":false}'```
Request ID from response header: `req_abc123`

alex-eng: Quick hypothesis — the SDK estimator only tokenizes the client-sent message array (user+system+assistant) locally. It does not include server-injected bytes used for runtime prefill (KV metadata) or tool-chain annotations that can be appended after request arrival. Metering/billing counts everything that reaches the model input after server-side rewrites and prefill. So if your request triggers KV prefill or tool output that gets reserialized into the prompt, invoice can be larger.

sre-jen: Also check streaming vs non-streaming behavior. If you use streaming and client aborts/resumes, duplicate completions can cause additional billed tokens. Any reconnects around that request?

customer-ops: Not for that particular request (we were non-streaming). The KV tool in our payload is small, but maybe the server expands it.

metering-bot: Metering event (debug): request_id=req_abc123 | client_tokens=15342 | server_injected_tokens=3778 | completion_tokens=21725 | billed_tokens=40845 | meter_version=2026-02-14

maya-support: The `server_injected_tokens` line is interesting — that means runtime added ~3.7k tokens to the model input. Two possibilities: (1) KV prefill expanded (large session context), (2) post-processing/annotation step appended tool metadata. Can you confirm whether you use session pinning or long-lived KV references?

customer-ops: We do pin session context for some users, but not thousands. For this test user session it's unexpected. How do I get the raw final prompt that the model saw?

alex-eng: You can request the raw resolved prompt from our debug endpoint (will only be available to account owners and requires `X-Debug-Metering: true`). Example:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "X-Debug-Metering: true" \n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/metering?request_id=req_abc123"``` That returns the tokenized counts and the resolved prompt (base64 or gzipped if large). Send that to support if you're comfortable.

maya-support: If you don't want to send raw prompt, paste the sizes from the debug response (client_tokens / server_injected_tokens / completion_tokens). We'll correlate with invoice lines.

customer-ops: Ran the debug call, here's redacted snippet:```text
resolved_prompt_preview: "[SYSTEM] You are a concise summarizer. [KV_PREFILL] {session_history: ... 12000 chars} [USER] Summarize the following logs..."
client_tokens: 15342
server_injected_tokens: 3778
completion_tokens: 21725```

maya-support: That preview confirms the prefill expanded with ~12k chars (explains the 3.7k tokens). This is not a billing error — invoice is correct. SDK estimator undercounted because it doesn't simulate server-side prefill.

customer-ops: Is there a recommended mitigation? We don't want surprise invoice jumps.

alex-eng: Options: (1) Reduce server-side prefill size by trimming session history or truncating KV values. (2) Use an SDK flag to request that server avoid automatic KV prefill for specific endpoints (we can enable per-account opt-out for prefill). (3) Use the Console to set max_prefill_tokens policy for your org. We can open a ticket to set conservative defaults for your workspace.

sre-jen: We'll also add an estimator improvement item: make the client estimator optionally include a safe upper-bound by pulling your account's prefill policy via `GET /v1/account/prefill-policy` and adding worst-case server_injected_tokens. For now, tell customers to use the debug endpoint periodically to reconcile.

customer-ops: Thanks — please open the opt-out ticket. Also can you add a note to the dashboard that shows "estimated server prefill" so users aren't blindsided? :eyes:

maya-support: Filed a ticket #SUP-4921 to opt-out and to add dashboard hint. We'll follow up with engineering on policy UI. :thumbsup:

customer-ops: Appreciate it — will await confirmation and update our SDK usage in the meantime.
